structural_root_cause.state_machine_gap: The kernel state machine has TWO places where current_round is set: critic_tasks_requested (line 1263) and cross_review_tasks_requested (line 1280). Both set state["current_round"] = payload["round_number"] when the kernel mints those tasks. BUT the revision_recorded reducer (line 1324 pre-fix) updated latest_revision and set state=REVISED — without touching current_round. The next P+C+CR cycle's submit_cross_review_v8 then read state["current_round"] = N (the round that PRODUCED the revision, not the round that should consume it) and tried to register tasks for round N. That round already had its cross_review in state["cross_reviews"][N] from the previous cycle, so _validate_cross_review_task_payload raised at line 1623.
structural_root_cause.lesson: Multi-round state machines require explicit round-advancement discipline. Each event that closes a round (revision_recorded, plan_evaluated, etc.) must either (a) advance the counter or (b) document the next-round computation is the consumer's responsibility. The pre-fix reducer was implicitly assuming the consumer would compute the next round, but submit_cross_review_v8 reads current_round directly with no offset logic.
structural_root_cause.tier_1_anchor: Same root pattern as F-021 (bridge mechanics) but at a different layer — F-021 was the BRIDGE_LAYER canonicalizer; F-022 is the STATE_MACHINE_LAYER counter discipline. Together they form the complete round-2 transition contract.

tier_1_architectural_fix.scope: kernel state machine — revision_recorded reducer now advances current_round
files_changed: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/plan_convergence.py (revision_recorded reducer at line 1324 adds state["current_round"] = payload["round"] + 1)

aria-kernel/tests/invariants/v10/test_phase_v10_4_phase_3_h_11_revision_round_advance.py (3 Tier-3 invariants — increment exists, lives in revision_recorded branch, uses payload["round"] anchor not hardcoded value)
tier_1_architectural_fix.tier_rationale: Tier-1 (make impossible): revision_recorded is the natural state-machine seam where 'next round begins'. By binding the counter advance to this reducer, the validator at _validate_cross_review_task_payload can no longer see a stale round_number from a consumer. The architectural truth ('recording a revision begins the next round') is now expressed structurally in the reducer, not implicitly in the consumer. Tier-3 (make detectable): the 3 invariants catch any future regression — increment missing, increment in wrong branch, increment with hardcoded value.

kernel_code_changes: 1-line state machine reducer addition. Plan_convergence main suite 28/28 green after fix — no regression. Existing single-round flows unaffected (they never reach revision_recorded). Multi-round flows now have correct counter discipline.

expected_impact_on_endurance.before_fix: cycle 1 of new endurance reached round-2 cross_review acceptance, then bridge_warning at fold layer. Plan state stuck at CHALLENGER_DRAFTED (round 2) — current_round stale at 1, cross_review tasks for round 1 already exist, validator rejects. Eventual cross_review_poll_timeout → convergence_blocked. Subsequent cycles 2-20 would hit the same wall.
expected_impact_on_endurance.after_fix: next round-2 cross_review submission post-revision will use current_round = 2 (or appropriate next number), state["cross_reviews"][2] is empty, validator accepts. State transitions CHALLENGER_DRAFTED → CROSS_REVIEW_REQUESTED → CROSS_REVIEWED (round 2) → verdict derivation. For CONVERGED verdict: implementation_requested fires → ARIA spawns aria-implementer → real PR creation.
